text:
Sam (AE): Heads-up — ACME is pushing on log retention & DSARs. They want all request/app logs purged within 30 days and proof we can remove any PII from logs on demand. Can we respond in the SIG/CAIQ and provide a DPA snippet? @Mira @Julian

Mira (Security): Short answer: hosted default is 180d for observability indices. We can offer contract-configurable retention, but true per-line deletion from immutable compressed logs is hard. Two realistic patterns: mask at ingestion (best), or allow deletion from processed indices (search layer) within an SLA.

Julian (Privacy): For DSARs we need to be able to either delete or render data non-identifiable. Customers often accept pseudonymization/hashing in logs plus an export of matching records if needed. For DPA language we should be explicit about what "deletion" means for logs vs user records.

Alex (Solutions): Proposed options to present to ACME: 1) Ingestion masking: remove/replace PII fields before write — supports 30d retention. 2) Configurable retention on processed indices (90/30/180d) + deletion job for matched DSARs (certified deletion report). 3) Private/Dedicated deployment for full control (if they need shorter or instant deletion). Also offer customer-managed export to SIEM for their retention rules.

Mira (Security): Technical constraints to call out in SIG answer: - "Logging & monitoring": retention configurable per contract; default 180d; masking available at ingestion to prevent PII landing in raw logs; deletion job removes entries from processed indices (SLA: up to 30 days to fully scrub from indices and caches). We should avoid promising immediate deletion from raw storage unless Dedicated/Private.

Julian (Privacy): Draft DPA clause suggestion (legal to refine): "Redwood will implement mutually agreed log retention and deletion procedures. For hosted deployments, logs containing customer data will be retained for the contractual retention period; Redwood will provide deletion or irreversible pseudonymization of customer-identifiable data upon request within the agreed SLA and certify completion."

Sam (AE): ACME says 30d is a hard requirement for request logs; 90d is ok for aggregated metrics. They asked for the exact SIG answer and a sample DPA clause today. Can Legal produce final language?

LegalBot: Uploaded draft DPA clause (see attached in thread). Key points included: retention configurable, masking/pseudonymization options, deletion certification, and an appendix for Dedicated deployments with full raw-log deletion.

Alex (Solutions): Sample config snippet to show ops team (for the RFP):
```
logs:
  request_logs:
    retention_days: 30
    mask_pii: true
    export_to_customer_siem: true
  audit_logs:
    retention_days: 90
```

Mira (Security): Implementation plan: - Implement masking at ingestion (config flag) - Add retention TTL on processed indices - Build DSAR deletion job that targets indices and search caches - Audit trail for deletion (cert)

Mira (Security): I've raised ENG ticket INF-1234 for masking & retention config (ETA 3w). DSAR deletion job tracked as INF-1235 (ETA +5w, but can be accelerated to +3w with scope cut).

Julian (Privacy): I'll do a quick review of Legal's clause and add the DSAR SLA (30d) language. If we can guarantee deletion certification within 30 days for processed indices, we're good to propose.

Sam (AE): OK — I'll present options to ACME: 30d on request logs with ingestion masking (preferred), 90d for audit metrics. I'll flag Dedicated as fallback. Also will mention small R&D timeline and a possible surcharge.

Alex (Solutions): Action items: - Mira: confirm INF-1234 & INF-1235 scope and any blockers. - Julian: approve DPA clause text. - LegalBot: finalize DPA appendix for logs. - Sam: share draft answers & config snippet with ACME and collect acceptance.

LegalBot: Noted. I'll attach final clause once Julian signs off.

Julian (Privacy): Approved with one small edit on the certification wording — will post the exact line shortly.

Mira (Security): No blockers from infra side. We'll need a short runbook for deletion requests (who owns what). I'll draft it and link to INF tickets.

Sam (AE): Thanks all — I'll loop back to ACME after Julian's edit. :thumbsup:
